messages:
alex: Heads up — our ingestion pipeline started failing when writing encrypted blobs to S3 this morning. Getting AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt after yesterday's CMK rotation. 

jess: Error snippet? which principal is doing the decrypt (service role vs assumed role)?

alex: CLI error from the worker pod: 
```
ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-worker-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```

alex: This worked right before the scheduled rotation. We rotate primary CMK nightly via our rotator job which creates a new key and rewraps envelopes. Something in the chain broke.

mira: Two common culprits: (1) the grant that allowed the assumed role to use the key didn't survive the rewrap/rotation flow, or (2) the key policy doesn't explicitly allow the assumed-role principal (and the grant path is relied on).

sam: Can you paste CloudTrail Decrypt event? Need the eventName, userIdentity.type, principalArn. Also check kms:CreateGrant events around rotation time.

alex: CloudTrail shows Decrypt AccessDenied. There is a CreateGrant during rotation but it looks like the grant was issued to the rotation Lambda's role, not to the ingest-worker role. We probably rekeyed envelopes but didn't recreate the grant for the worker.

jess: Ah — we had logic that reassigns grants only to roles listed in a static config. The ingest service was on the deprecated ARN (we migrated to assume-role pattern). Grant creation skipped it.

sam: Quick mitigation: create a grant that allows the current assumed-role principal to Decrypt and RetireGrant. Example: 
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/production-ingest-key \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-worker-role \
  --operations Decrypt RetireGrant GenerateDataKey --name "ingest-grant-temp"
```
Note: if caller is an assumed role, you may need to pass --grant-tokens if using a grant token workflow from earlier operations.

mira: Also double-check key policy: if it uses a condition restricting "aws:PrincipalArn" patterns or only allows specific AWS accounts/principals, ensure the assumed-role ARN (sts format) is permitted. Key policy should allow the role or the account to use grants.

alex: I created the grant using sam's command and workers resumed. Patch applied to rotator to also create grants for the ingest role after rotation.

jess: For the permanent fix, recommend: (1) update rotator to enumerate current active principals (including assumed roles) and re-create grants, (2) add an explicit statement in the key policy allowing the ingest role to use the CMK (or allow kms:CreateGrant by the rotator role), and (3) add CloudTrail alarm for CreateGrant/RetireGrant anomalies.

mira: Policy snippet we used to land (replace ARNs): 
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowIngestRole","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-worker-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"} ]}
```

alex: FYI we kept audit log of the rotator's actions (CreateGrant / RetireGrant) in a ticket. Also added a unit test in rotator that simulates an assumed-role principal and ensures grants are created.

infra-bot: Deploy of rotator v2 finished in prod — rolling restart of ingestion pods to pick up role mapping.

jess: Follow-up: do we need to consider envelope rewrap ordering? If rewrap happened before granting, ingesters could see a short window of failure. Rotator should create grants for consumers before swapping envelopes.

sam: Good catch. Added ordering: create grants -> rewrap -> retire old grants. Also added retry logic on CreateGrant.

alex: Closing this thread — root cause: rotator omitted ingest role when recreating grants during CMK rotation. Resolved by manual grant + rotator fix. Filing postmortem with timeline and CloudTrail evidence. :white_check_mark:
